name: Chlorine and pool chemicals
summary: Bleach and pool chlorine: liquid sodium hypochlorite, calcium hypochlorite granules and chlorine tablets.
uses: Disinfecting clear drinking water: 2 drops (0.1 mL) of plain 5 to 9 % bleach per litre, wait 30 minutes, double it for cloudy water (CDC); below 10 °C, double it and wait 1 to 2 hours (HealthLinkBC 49b)

Does not kill Cryptosporidium (Health Canada protozoa); generally not effective against Giardia (HealthLinkBC 10). For lake, river and pond water, boil it or use a filter rated for cysts, absolute 1 micron or finer (HealthLinkBC 10), then add chlorine to keep it protected in storage (Sphere)

Measuring tiny doses: a 1 mL oral or tuberculin syringe marked in mL beats counting drops: CDC and HealthLinkBC 49b count 2 drops as 0.1 mL, Health Canada as 0.2 mL (Health Canada emergency). On a U-100 insulin syringe, 100 units is 1 mL, so 10 units is 0.1 mL (ADA insulin); keep its needle capped

For a 20 L (5 US gal) bucket, measure 2.5 mL of 5 to 9 % bleach once (CDC), pour it into a bottle cap or small cup, mark the level and use that mark from then on. Keep the syringe and cup for bleach only, and label them
identify: Bleach in homes, shops and laundries; buckets of granules (calcium hypochlorite) and tablets (often trichlor) at pool shops, pool plant rooms, hotels and farm stores. For drinking water use only plain bleach or calcium hypochlorite, with no scent, algaecide or stabiliser.
test: Read the label for strength: bleach is about 3–8%, granules about 65–70%. Never mix with acids, ammonia or other chemicals, which gives off toxic gas, and keep granules away from oil and fuel: together they can catch fire.

decay.note: Clorox says bleach keeps up to a year cool, dry and out of the sun, then breaks down fast (Clorox date); EPA says use bleach under a year old (EPA water). EPA gives calcium hypochlorite 24 months tightly closed, cool and dry (EPA cal hypo). Check old bleach as the guide Test bleach strength shows.
